summary: A 1970 report on a network meeting, written by Jon Postel. It records the discussion.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 77 reports on three Network Working Group meetings held in Houston in November 1970. It records discussion about protocol testing, TELNET, documentation, graphics, resource accounting, and user interaction.

questions: what did the network working group discuss in houston
what was discussed about telnet in 1970
subtitle: Jon Postel's report on Network Working Group meetings in Houston.

tldr.problem: Network Working Group participants needed to share the topics and proposals discussed at their November meetings.
tldr.mechanism: Jon Postel's report records the subjects raised, points of discussion, and proposals made during three meetings at the Fall Joint Computer Conference.
tldr.outcome: RFC 77 is a meeting report that documents early network discussions; it is not a protocol specification.

today: RFC 77 is a report on early Network Working Group meetings. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that updates or replaces it.

sections.title: Topics for Network Development
sections.content:
The report lists seven topics of concern: independent protocol testing; improvements to the Host-Host protocol; a TELNET specification; documentation; graphics; resource accounting; and network measurement.

It describes TELNET as a needed higher-level program for logging in to remote hosts, running programs, transferring files, and calling for help.
sections.plainLanguage: The participants identified practical work needed for the network, including testing protocols, remote login, documentation, and accounting.

sections.title: Protocol Changes and Network Information
sections.content:
Participants generally favored making protocol changes in groups about six months apart, with about three months of lead time. They approved a proposed change to remove marking from the IMP-Host protocol but said implementation should wait rather than happen as a casual change.

The report records support for getting teletype-like remote console use working before graphics. It also describes the Network Information Center's work to make information about the network and hosts available to users.
sections.plainLanguage: The group preferred planned batches of protocol changes and prioritized remote console use over graphics. It also discussed making network and host documentation available.

sections.title: Console Interaction and File Transfer
sections.content:
The meetings discuss differences between half-duplex and full-duplex consoles and between line-oriented and character-oriented interaction. The report describes these as difficulties when users connect to hosts with different systems.

The participants also discuss how to mark message and file boundaries, count bytes, and coordinate file transfer. The meeting ends with a request for participants to circulate further ideas and proposals.
sections.plainLanguage: The report records open questions about consoles and file transfer. Participants were asked to continue proposing solutions in later notes.
